additions.title: Uncertainty-aware physics-informed neural networks for the wear detection of friction pairs in axial piston pumps
An ultrafast response non-contact method based on flexible photovoltaic sensor for high-precision bridge deflection monitoring under low-frequency vibrations
additions.abstract: Precise deflection monitoring is imperative for the evaluation of the structural safety and long-term serviceability of long-span bridges. However, conventional contact and non-contact deflection sensing techniques frequently encounter issues with installation complexity, environmental sensitivity, and limited applicability for long-term field deployment. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a non-contact deflection sensing method based on a flexible graphene-silicon photovoltaic sensor (GS-PVS). Configured as an ultrathin Schottky junction film, the sensor enables conformal integration with complex or deformable surfaces while maintaining electro-optical stability under bending, stretching, and compression, thereby supporting stable and high-fidelity sensing of structural deflection. Utilizing the photovoltaic effect, the system converts displacement-induced variations in light intensity into short-circuit current, which is quantitatively correlated to structural deflection via an analytical sensing model. Experimental validation demonstrates a rapid response time of approximately 30 μs and high measurement accuracy over a low-frequency range of 0.1–3 Hz, with deviations within 5% compared with those of a commercial laser displacement sensor. The system also maintains stable performance under varying illumination and geometric conditions through baseline correction and incidence-angle compensation. This work offers a compact, cost-effective, and robust sensing strategy for direct and quantitative deflection monitoring, providing an effective complement to existing techniques for structural health monitoring of long-span bridges.

additions.title: Biomineralization for sealing jagged microfracture: Effect of pH on crystallization kinetics
additions.abstract: Jagged microfractures (aperture <1 mm) are widespread in caprocks and pose a threat to the sealing effectiveness and long-term stability of geological carbon sequestration (GCS). Biomineralization provides a promising strategy for sealing such microfractures. However, underground solutions typically vary with pH, and the sealing performance of biomineralization is highly sensitive to pH. Consequently, its effectiveness under different grouting pH conditions remains unclear. This study addresses the research gap by conducting microfluidic fracture-sealing tests to elucidate the effects of pH on crystallization processes and sealing patterns. The number of grain boundaries, crystal count, and irregularity of CaCO 3 crystals exhibit an initial increasing trend with pH, but then decrease above pH 6.5. Crystal size exhibited the opposite trend. A modified logistic model adequately characterized the temporal evolution of CaCO 3 content, with a goodness of fit greater than 0.93. Meanwhile, the Arrhenius growth model effectively captured the variation in the maximum precipitation rate with pH, with a goodness of fit value of 0.955. The optimal pH range was determined as 5.5–6.5 to enhance jagged microfracture sealing efficiency and achieve a permeability reduction ratio exceeding 94%. These findings indicate that the pH is pivotal to regulating the sealing behavior of jagged microfractures and provide practical guidance for applying biomineralization to microfracture sealing in GCS.

additions.title: Machine learning modelling for directly identifying highly toxic organic contaminants from wastewater based on high-resolution mass spectrometry
additions.abstract: Identifying highly toxic contaminants in environmental matrices is critical for effective risk management and control. Nontarget screening coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) is the most widely used tool for this purpose. However, conventional nontarget analysis is unnecessarily complex, as it requires structural identification of multiple features before assessing toxicity. To address this, we developed machine learning models that directly predict toxicity from spectral data, enabling early detection of toxic features before structural elucidation. By integrating acute toxicity data from four fish species, we expanded the datasets by 1.26–4.23 folds and 1.55–4.97 folds in positive and negative ion modes, respectively, compared to the single-species dataset. The optimized models achieved RMSE test values of 0.29 (positive mode) and 0.30 (negative mode), indicating an average predicted deviation within 2 folds for the test sets. We then applied these models to predict acute toxicity for nontargeted features detected by HRMS in municipal and hospital wastewater samples. Over 68.51% of features were filtered out as non-highly toxic by our models quickly, leaving 540 (municipal) and 4696 (hospital) highly toxic features (LC 50 <1 mg/L) for further structural analysis. Among these, 186 were successfully identified with definitive structures. In addition, surface water and soil samples were employed for validation and application of our models in other environmental matrices. In summary, this study presents a novel nontarget screening approach to prioritize highly toxic chemicals in environmental samples, significantly improving the efficiency of high-risk pollutant identification and risk assessment.

additions.title: EnerPF-LLM: Long-term prediction for probability distribution of renewable power with lightweight language models
additions.abstract: The increasing penetration of wind and photovoltaic generation adds considerable uncertainty to power system operations, underscoring the need for accurate and uncertainty-aware prediction. The strong stochasticity and spatial correlations of renewable resources limit deterministic point predictions, while practical operations depend on probabilistic predictions to assess risk. Although recent deep learning models capture temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies, graph neural network (GNN)-based approaches often treat meteorological extreme events as shallow features, making it difficult to learn higher-level semantic factors and leading to unstable calibrated predictions. Large language models offer complementary semantic modeling capabilities but remain limited in capturing node-level heterogeneity. To address this gap, we propose EnerPF-large language model (LLM), a unified probabilistic prediction framework that integrates LLM-based semantic temporal modeling with adaptive graph-based spatio-temporal learning. Historical power observations and dataset statistical descriptors are tokenized and aligned with a pre-trained LLM to extract regional semantic trend priors, while an adaptive graph learning module generates node-level predictive distributions. Experiments on public wind and photovoltaic (PV) benchmarks indicate that EnerPF-LLM offers improvements in both point and probabilistic metrics over representative deep learning baselines, and ablation studies highlight the complementary roles of semantic prior modeling. This study provides an example of combining semantic modeling with spatial heterogeneity in probabilistic renewable prediction and may inform future work on extreme weather adaptation, multi-modal meteorological integration, and regional energy management.

additions.title: A surgical palpation probe with MEMS-based 3D force sensing for robot-assisted surgery
additions.abstract: Although tissue palpation is a critical clinical procedure, it cannot be performed directly in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (RMIS) due to remote operation and an enclosed surgical environment. This study presents a surgical palpation probe for RMIS, integrated with a MEMS-based three-dimensional (3D) piezoresistive force sensor. The sensor comprises a MEMS chip featuring four piezoresistive micro-bridge architectures and a PDMS-based force transmission layer, enabling high-accuracy detection of both normal and lateral forces. A key innovation is the co-design of the MEMS sensor with a novel parallelogram-structured transmission shell, which uniquely provides simultaneous effective force transmission, intrinsic overload protection, and biocompatible encapsulation. These three features are critical for clinical translation but have not been addressed in prior studies. Comprehensive experiments validate the good linearity, low hysteresis (< 4.38%), and fast response (< 10 ms) of the probe. Robotic palpation trials using simulated cancerous and vascular tissues demonstrate sub-millimeter localization accuracy and high recognition fidelity when force contour mapping is implemented. Furthermore, the palpation forces are delivered to the operator via real-time haptic feedback. In a user study conducted under a teleoperation framework, participants without clinical backgrounds achieved 90% accuracy in identifying tumors and blood vessels after only 5 min of training. These findings support the clinical potential of the probe in RMIS for real-time intraoperative tissue characterization and intuitive surgeon feedback.

additions.title: Phosphorus doping enhances built-in electrical fields in NiCo/P-Ti3CNTx heterojunctions for superior alkaline hydrogen evolution in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers
additions.abstract: The construction of heterojunctions that generate a built-in electric field (BIEF) at the interface has been demonstrated as an effective strategy for accelerating hydrogen evolution reaction kinetics. However, conventional heterojunctions typically exhibit insufficient BIEF strength, resulting in suboptimal electrocatalytic performance. Herein, we present a phosphorus-doping strategy to precisely enhance the BIEF strength within a NiCo/P-Ti 3 CNT x heterojunction. It is demonstrated that substantially increasing the work function difference between NiCo and Ti 3 CNT x enables P doping to remarkably enhance interfacial charge transfer and accelerate hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) kinetics. The NiCo/P-Ti 3 CNT x catalyst is synthesized via a two-step process involving Lewis acid-assisted dual molten salt etching followed by low-temperature phosphatization. The NiCo/P-Ti 3 CNT x demonstrates an overpotential of merely 90 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm −2 and maintains stable operation for 30 h at a current density of 200 mA cm −2 . In an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, when utilized as the cathode, it exhibits a current density of 350 mA cm −2 at 1.73 V with exceptional durability exceeding 200 h. These findings substantiate the efficacy of P doping as a methodology for enhancing BIEF strength and facilitating interfacial electron transfer, providing a rational pathway toward efficient and durable nonprecious-metal catalysts for sustainable hydrogen production.

additions.title: KDF-Mimic: From kinematic retargeting to dynamic feasibility for robust humanoid motion imitation
Event-based fully distributed secure control of multiagent systems with asynchronous attacks
additions.abstract: A secure consensus control issue of multiagent systems (MASs) with asynchronous denial-of-service (DoS) attacks is tackled by using a fully distributed event-triggered (ET) strategy. In view of asynchronous DoS attacks, we categorize DoS attacks into three modes by introducing the Fiedler value. To ensure that the more reliable signals are obtained when the DoS attack appears, an observer is established to compensate for the missing signals. Then, an ET mechanism is designed by combining with the compensation information, which not only removes the requirement of continuous communication, but also maintains the normal operation in spite of losing the neighbor information. Further, a sufficient condition is given to guarantee the system stability by virtue of the designed fully distributed control approach. Moreover, the Zeno behavior is demonstrated by a strict proof. The effectiveness of the presented scheme is validated via the numerical simulation.

additions.title: Homotopy-based reinforcement learning for distributed optimal consensus of multi-agent systems under adversarial inputs and fuzzy imprecise topologies
additions.abstract: This paper presents an innovative distributed optimal consensus control framework for multi-agent systems operating with adversarial inputs under imprecise communication topologies, modeled through Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy graphs. Departing from conventional approaches that mandate connected subgraphs for each fuzzy rule, our methodology accommodates disconnected network configurations while guaranteeing consensus through a weak fuzzy union connectivity condition. We propose a distributed homotopy-based reinforcement learning architecture, namely a distributed two-stage reinforcement learning framework, which comprises (1) a data-based homotopy policy iteration algorithm and (2) an enhanced integral Q -learning scheme, both capable of deriving stabilizing control policies from arbitrary initial conditions without requiring prior system knowledge. The proposed framework maintains rigorous stability, optimality, and guaranteed L 2 gain performance. The numerical simulation on an F-404 aircraft engine system demonstrates the superior efficacy of our approach in achieving consensus amidst topological uncertainties and adversarial inputs.

additions.title: Dual-mechanism vibration suppression in a nonlinear metamaterial hyperelastic pipe conveying fluid
additions.abstract: Traditional linear meta-structures often suffer from limited vibration attenuation and narrow band gap (BG) widths, restricting their broader engineering applications. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a nonlinear metamaterial hyperelastic pipe conveying fluid that integrates coupled geometric-material nonlinearities and nonlinear stiffness, forming a dual-mechanism vibration suppression strategy. It is demonstrated that although the coupled nonlinearities induced by hyperelasticity can modify the dispersion characteristics, their contribution to BG expansion is relatively limited. However, it effectively reduces vibration amplitudes and shifts resonance peaks toward higher frequencies, which is advantageous for low-frequency operation. In contrast, the introduction of periodic nonlinear resonators substantially broadens the BG, thereby enhancing vibration suppression performance. The study also indicates that tuning the resonator amplitude can manipulate the dispersion relation, exhibiting the amplitude-dependent band structure behavior of nonlinear metamaterials and thereby further improving the bandwidth. Nevertheless, for such fluid-structure interaction (FSI) systems, when the flow velocity increases sufficiently to drive the system into a supercritical regime, the BG will disappear, and the vibration suppression capability of the meta-structure is lost. Overall, the present design provides a novel and efficient dual-mechanism vibration control strategy for engineering pipeline structures conveying fluid.

additions.title: Tubular Sr-doped g-C3N4 loading upconversion nanoparticles towards enhanced photocatalytic antibacterial properties of bone scaffold
additions.abstract: The penetration depth of ultraviolet-visible light used to drive photosensitizers in human tissues is relatively shallow, limiting the photocatalytic antibacterial effect of the bone scaffold. In contrast, near-infrared (NIR) light has a stronger ability to penetrate tissues, but traditional photosensitizers cannot directly respond to it. In this study, NaYF 4 :Yb,Tm (NYF) upconversion nanoparticle was loaded on the surface of tubular Sr-doped g-C 3 N 4 (TCN-Sr) by electrostatic self-assembly method, and then incorporated into poly(l-lactic acid) (PLLA) to fabricate PLLA/TCN-Sr@NYF bone scaffold through selective laser sintering (SLS). Under the excitation of 980 nm NIR light, Yb 3+ acted as a photosensitizer, absorbing photon energy, transitioning from the 2 F 7/2 ground state to the 2 F 5/2 excited state, and gradually transferring the energy to Tm 3+ . The excited-state Tm 3+ returned to the lower energy state by emitting low-wavelength light of 365 and 479 nm, which corresponded to the 1 D 2 → 3 H 6 and 1 G 4 → 3 H 6 transitions within Tm 3+ , respectively. TCN-Sr could effectively absorb blue-violet light with wavelengths of 365 and 479 nm, thus leading to the generation of electron-hole pairs and producing reactive oxygen species. The results of the in vitro antibacterial assay indicated that the antibacterial rates of the PLLA/TCN-Sr@NYF scaffold against S. aureus and E. coli reached 92.5% and 96.0%, respectively. The in vitro cell experiment results demonstrated that the scaffold possessed excellent biocompatibility and could support the growth and proliferation of cells.
